responses: Hello! Welcome to CyberSafe AI. How can I help you stay safe online?
Phishing is a scam where attackers use fake emails, messages, or websites to steal personal information.
Warning signs include suspicious links, urgent requests, unexpected attachments, and fake login pages.
Never enter passwords or OTPs on unverified websites. Verify the sender and open official websites directly.
If you entered your password on a suspicious website, change it immediately using the official website and secure your account.
An OTP scam occurs when someone tricks you into revealing a one-time password to access an account or authorize an action.
Never share your OTP with callers, messages, or people claiming to be bank officials.
If you already shared an OTP, secure the affected account immediately. Contact your bank through its official channel if financial information or transactions are involved.
If money was lost through financial cyber fraud in India, call 1930 promptly and report the incident at https://cybercrime.gov.in/.
A job scam involves fake recruiters or employers who try to steal money or personal information.
Warning signs include requests for recruitment fees, unrealistic salaries, vague job descriptions, and pressure to act immediately.
Verify the vacancy on the company's official careers website and contact the company using its official contact details.

If you already paid a suspected scammer, preserve the messages and payment records. Contact your bank or payment provider and report financial cyber fraud in India through 1930 and https://cybercrime.gov.in/.
UPI fraud occurs when someone tricks you into authorizing a payment or revealing sensitive financial information.
You do not need to enter your UPI PIN to receive money. Review unexpected collect requests carefully before approving them.
If an unauthorized transaction occurs, contact your bank and UPI service provider immediately.
For financial cyber fraud in India, call 1930 promptly and report it at https://cybercrime.gov.in/. Keep your transaction ID and evidence.
Investment scams use false promises of profits to persuade people to transfer money.
Warning signs include guaranteed high returns, pressure to invest quickly, and requests to transfer money to personal accounts.
Verify the company and relevant registration through official regulatory sources before investing.
If you have already transferred money, preserve evidence, contact your bank or payment provider, and report suspected financial fraud.
An online shopping scam involves a fake seller or website that may take payment without delivering the promised product.
Check seller reviews, contact details, return policies, and website authenticity before paying.
If an order does not arrive, contact the seller and payment provider through official channels and preserve receipts and messages.
Report suspected financial cyber fraud in India through 1930 and https://cybercrime.gov.in/.
For cybercrime reporting in India, call the national cybercrime helpline at 1930, especially if you have lost money through financial cyber fraud.
You can submit an online complaint through the official National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal: https://cybercrime.gov.in/.
Keep relevant evidence such as transaction IDs, screenshots, phone numbers, messages, and dates. Never share your passwords or OTPs in a complaint to an unverified person.
If your account has been hacked, use the platform's official account recovery process immediately.
Change your password from a trusted device, secure your linked email account, enable two-factor authentication, and sign out of unfamiliar sessions if possible.
Do not pay someone who promises guaranteed account recovery. Contact the platform through its official support channels.
If the incident involves financial loss, contact your bank immediately and report it through the appropriate official cybercrime channels.
Online harassment, threats, or blackmail should be taken seriously. Your safety comes first, and you are not to blame for another person's abusive behavior.
Save screenshots, profile links, messages, dates, and other evidence when it is safe to do so.
Block or report the account using the platform's official reporting tools. Avoid sending money or additional private information to someone threatening you.
If you are in immediate danger, contact local police or emergency services. In India, you can also report cybercrime at https://cybercrime.gov.in/.
Identity theft occurs when someone misuses your personal information to impersonate you or access services.
Secure affected accounts, change compromised passwords, enable two-factor authentication, and contact relevant banks or service providers if financial details are involved.
Preserve evidence and report fake profiles through the relevant platform's official reporting tools.
If financial cyber fraud has occurred in India, call 1930 promptly and report it at https://cybercrime.gov.in/.
Malware is malicious software designed to damage devices, steal information, or gain unauthorized access.
Warning signs may include unexpected pop-ups, unfamiliar applications, unusual account activity, or unexplained device behavior.
Avoid opening suspicious files or links. Update your operating system, remove suspicious applications, and use reputable security software.
If you suspect an account password was stolen, change it from a trusted device and secure the affected accounts.
